replacement.title: Python for Everybody (PY4E)
replacement.evidence: Site: materials are free; 'free, global open and online course'; CC BY 4.0.
replacement.why: Beginner Python course with no prior programming required, progressing to files, web data and APIs — same goal and level as IBM's Python for Data Science, AI & Development.
replacement.gap: No pandas/NumPy unit; Kaggle Learn Python + pandas User Guide (both on the source roadmap) fill this.

replacement.title: Ben Lambert: A full course in econometrics – undergraduate level (YouTube)
replacement.evidence: Public playlist, 199 videos. Ben Lambert's channel (@SpartacanUsuals) confirmed; the fetched playlist page reported its owner as 'newtvchannel', so whether this playlist is hosted on Ben Lambert's own channel is NOT confirmed.
replacement.why: Advanced-undergraduate econometrics: OLS, Gauss-Markov, inference, heteroskedasticity/serial-correlation tests, IV/2SLS and time series (stationarity, unit roots, cointegration) — the same scope and level as Erasmus's course.
replacement.gap: Binary-choice (logit/probit) models are not in part 1; playlist ownership unconfirmed.

replacement.title: mlcourse.ai Topics 1–2: EDA with Pandas and Visual Data Analysis
replacement.evidence: Course pages open without login; no licence/price statement on page; some bonus assignments are behind a Patreon tier. Topics 1–2 cover data cleaning, preliminary analysis and plotting with Seaborn/Matplotlib/Plotly.
replacement.why: Hands-on, beginner-to-intermediate pandas EDA on real datasets — same goal as the 2-hour Coursera Guided Project. Already on the source roadmap (Machine Learning topic).
replacement.gap: Not a single 2-hour project; learners should use Topics 1–2 only.

replacement.title: Computational and Inferential Thinking (UC Berkeley Data 8 textbook)
replacement.evidence: Site: 'licensed for free consumption' under CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Chapters include Sampling, Testing Hypotheses, Comparing Two Samples, Estimation, Inference for Regression — all in Python.
replacement.why: Beginner-level statistics taught in Python (sampling, hypothesis tests, A/B-style two-sample comparison, estimation, regression inference) — the same goal as UMich's Statistics with Python.
replacement.gap: No Bayesian or multilevel-model material (UMich course 3 touches these).
